text:
Nils Hoglander went between his legs and top shelf for the go-ahead goal in Anaheim on Wednesday, the one NHL.com and ClutchPoints floated as a goal-of-the-year candidate, in a 4-2 win that made it six straight for Nashville. After 331 games as a Canuck, he has 9 points in 20 games as a Predator, mostly on fourth-line minutes (11.07 a night).

Some of it is bounces. The Predators have scored 6.89 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and his points rate (2.44 per 60) is above the top of our talent range. But the chances are real: 1.05 expected goals per 60 on his own shots (a measure of chance quality), more than double his 0.47 in Vancouver last season, and 4 goals on 3.87 expected is honest finishing. Nashville gets 52.2% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, 6.6 points better than without him. His ice time has run between 13 and 15 minutes in each of the last four games. Last season's numbers came on a small sample (438 minutes, per Evolving-Hockey), so this is the longest look we've had at him in a real role.
headline: Nils Hoglander's highlight goal and a bigger role
